thread:
maria: heads-up: on the 2k token short-seq bench I'm still seeing ~14ms of host-side overhead before the model starts decoding. baseline last week was ~6ms.
aj: hmm, did you re-run with the new grpc window patch?
maria: yeah, same numbers. took a quick flamegraph on the host and it spikes in the parse->tokenize path.
kevin: can you paste the flame snippet? might be writev/coalesce churn or extra memcpy from protobuf decode.
maria: here — truncated output:
```
flamegraph: host_parse (14ms)
  ├─ grpc/frame_unwrap 4.1ms
  ├─ proto::DeserializeRequest 3.6ms
  ├─ utf8_normalize 2.8ms
  └─ tokenizer::encode_batch 3.5ms
```
olga: my first gut is gRPC frame reassembly + smallwrites. HTTP2/hpack can add headroom for small streaming chunks.
aj: also check KV cache lookup noise — if tokenization emits many tiny prefix writes we thrash the kvcache hotset and reserialize headers.
maria: ran a quick trace; kvcache hits drop from 98%->89% under the short-seq pattern. looks correlated with the tokenizer producing variable-length prefixes.
kevin: interesting — maybe the tokenizer pool is allocating buffers per request. can you capture allocations?
maria: attached quick pprof snapshot (copied inline):
```
# pprof heap
100k tokenizer::encode_buffer
60k proto::TmpBuf
20k grpc::slice
```
kevin: yep allocation churn. try reusing a per-thread scratch for encode buffer and consolidate small writes into a single writev per stream. should help both allocs and writev pressure.
aj: on kernel selection side, we saw similar host overhead when switching quant kernels last month — kernel choice affected batch shape and led to more small RPCs. could be the runtime now choosing a smaller kernel for short sequences and increasing host preproc fraction.
maria: experiment: pinned kernel to 'fast-smallseq-v2' and ran bench: host overhead dropped to 9-10ms, kvcache back to 95% hit. model decode begins earlier too.
olga: partial mitigation. still 4ms higher than baseline though. what about batching hints? if the incoming request stream isn't being coalesced because chunk boundaries are too fine, we pay framing overhead.
maria: true — current ingress chunker emits whenever we hit 512 bytes or newline. for short prompts it's often <512 so we flush, causing tiny frames.
aj: propose: adaptive chunker that waits up to X ms to coalesce small frames unless latency SLO for that route is strict. X should be route-configurable. we can also floor the header flush so writev merges the proto + body.
kevin: +1. impl plan: (1) reuse per-thread encoder buffer, (2) single writev per request, (3) adaptive chunk coalescer with route SLO override.
maria: I'll prototype 1+2 today. can I get someone to own the adaptive chunker heuristics?
olga: I'll take heuristics and SLO gating. will sketch thresholds and rollout canary.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: eng-runtime/host-preproc-coalesce v1 -> canary cluster in 30m.
maria: awesome. once I have a patch I'll attach a micro-benchmark. expected win: 3-7ms host savings on short seqs, improved kvcache locality.
aj: don't forget to add telemetry for 'frames_per_request' and 'avg_writev_count'. those will tell us if coalescing is effective.
kevin: and a regression test that simulates jittered small writes. last time the fix regressed large-batch throughput.
maria: noted. I'll open PR and link perf runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
